newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russian defence minister warns NATO on expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister warns NATO on expansion.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said in an interview released on Wednesday that the Russian population would force politicians and the military to take "appropriate measures" if NATO's eastward expansion goes ahead.
Rodionov told the German magazine Stern that NATO's plans would undermine the confidence carefully built up between Russia and the alliance.

Asked what Moscow would do if expansion plans went ahead despite Russian opposition, he said: "We would have to react with appropriate measures. The people would force the politicians and the military to do so."
He continued: "The rejection of NATO expansion is a matter of principle and independent from the political situation."
He said Russia was working out "different variations" on its response but did not go into any detail.
Rodionov said it was difficult for Russia to rely purely on the goodwill of its allies. "The fount of positive feelings towards the West is not unlimited," he said.
"How can Russia rely on the assurances from its western partners, when they previously promised not to expand NATO eastwards?" he asked in the interview, released ahead of publication on Thursday.
